discussion_comments.comment_body: `convert_base_loc` now copies `base.start` into `start_offset`, but one path doesn't keep a real offset in `base.start`. Before an outlined JSX component is lowered, `build_outlined_scope_info` in `entrypoint/pipeline.rs` (lines 1237, 1345, 1489, 1548, 1571) writes placeholder positions there, and those now reach the output. With `--rust`, `jsx-outlining-child-stored-in-id.js` gives the `Baz` tag in `_temp` `start: 7, end: 190`, while `loc.start.index` is 187. TS gives 187. I see this on 36 `JSXIdentifier` nodes in 9 of the 10 `jsx-outlining-*` fixtures. Reference lookup already uses `node_id`. Could that path keep the real `start`, or clear `start_offset`?

The outlined scope helper now uses node_id for identity and preserves the original offsets. Three regression tests cover shifted/absent offsets, colliding ranges, and nested JSX bindings. The range check passes across all 1,832 Rust fixtures.

+//! A JavaScript string value. JS strings are sequences of UTF-16 code units
+//! with no validity requirement, so a value can contain unpaired surrogate
+//! halves that Rust's `String` cannot represent. `JsString` keeps the common
+//! valid case as UTF-8 and falls back to code units only when the value is
+//! ill-formed, so the compiler computes on true program values instead of
+//! replacement characters or escape hatches.
+//!
+//! Wire format: the babel bridge transports lone surrogates as
+//! `__SURROGATE_XXXX__` markers (see `sanitizeJsonSurrogates` in bridge.ts),
+//! because serde_json can neither parse nor emit a lone `\uXXXX` escape.
+//! Serde for `JsString` decodes and re-emits that marker form, which keeps the
+//! JS side of the bridge unchanged.

+use std::fmt;
+
+use serde::Deserialize;
+use serde::Serialize;
+

+pub enum JsString {
